# EXIT_MGMT_SUNDAY_MATCH (W-DYNA for W-SUNDAY; generated 27 Nov 20:42Z UTC): per-second match rows for BE70 / PL70K50 / NT70K25

Source: exact trades of TL3_DX_<S>_<MF>_sun_<code>_M (all 42 months done, W-SUNDAY) + the 1-s NQ table (tables/NQ/1s: last, hi, lo, bid, ask per second; the engine evaluates the rule on EVERY PRINT, so a 1-s row can arm / touch up to one second earlier or later than the engine: the exact engine times are given beside each trade). Rule definitions (EXIT_MGMT_KEYS.md, dx_multi.py): T0 = the book's target distance, best = best favourable excursion since entry; BE70: once best >= 0.7 x T0 the resting stop goes to entry (rounded to the tick), ratchet only; PL70K50: once best >= 0.7 x T0 the stop sits at entry + 0.5 x best (tick rounded, ratchet); NT70K25: once best >= 0.7 x T0 the stop trails at best - 0.25 x T0 (ratchet); the original target stays; at 1/2/3/6 lots the whole position follows the stop. Columns: ts_s (epoch s of the second), last, hi, lo, bid, ask, best_pts (running best from hi for a long / lo for a short since the entry second), best_over_T0, armed, stop_level (the initial stop = entry -/+ S0 before arming), stop_touched (the second's low <= stop for a long, high >= stop for a short), in_trade. The engine row below each table is the exact-engine exit (time, price, name): the stop fill is NOT at the level when the market gaps through (engine fill model, hair 0.5 / LAT_FILL 1.0 s). The tape rows are decimated (every 3rd kept of a 1-5 s sample; all rows within 3 s of the arming second, every row with the stop touched, and the last 10 rows).

Selection: BE70 on each edge book, two trades where the rule fires and the stop is hit: SAVED = the own bracket would have hit its STOP afterwards (the rule saved a loss) and COST = the own bracket would have reached its TARGET afterwards (the rule cut a winner); NY-FIB and NY-NODE also get one PL70K50 and one NT70K25 trade (a profitable stop-out). The median-dated qualifying trade of each kind, lasting 3-240 minutes (rows decimated: every 5th second, every 6th-10th second for long trades).

# LANDSCAPE MATCH TRADES (W-SUNDAY-LS, 28 Nov): give-back cap and trail rows

Rules as coded (code/th_ls/ls_mgr.py, dx_algo hook): both are RESTING-STOP ratchets (dx_algo `_ratchet`: b.stop_px and the stop order price move to the tick-rounded level at every print, only tightening; the fill is an ordinary Stop through the engine stop fill model). g67a70: once best favourable excursion >= 0.7 x T0 the stop sits at entry + 0.67 x best (peaklock arm_R = 0.7 x T0/S0 in risk units). tr100: once best >= 0.5 x T0 the stop trails best - 1.0 x S0 points (k_R = 1.0 in units of the STOP distance risk0, NOT of the target distance). The book has no target (events tgt_pts NaN). The stop level per second below is reconstructed from the rule on the 1-s tape (hi / lo of the second); the engine applies it on every print, so a move can be up to one second earlier in the engine. Columns: ts_s, last, hi, lo, bid, ask, best_pts (running best excursion from hi for a long / lo for a short since the entry second), armed, stop_level, stop_moved (1 = this second raised the stop), in_trade. Rows kept: the first 3, the arming window, every second with a stop move and its neighbours (thinned when long), the last 8.
